Optimal.Notes: The Deck's GPU comfortably handles EU4 at native resolution with high textures and moderate AA; the 8 W TDP keeps thermals and fan noise low. This is the recommended daily-driver profile for long campaign sessions.

profiles.Summary: Europa Universalis IV is a lightweight grand strategy title from 2013 with very modest GPU demands, making it an excellent fit for the Steam Deck — the hardware far exceeds the minimum and recommended specs. ProtonDB reports trend platinum, suggesting it runs well under Proton with minimal fuss, though the lack of native controller support means keyboard/mouse input via the Deck's trackpads will be essential.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the 2013 PC minimum/recommended requirements (well below Deck capability), ProtonDB's platinum trend, and the game's known CPU-simulation-bound nature. On first run, verify the Proton version launches correctly, check UI text legibility, and monitor CPU frame time in late-game large saves where simulation load peaks.

MaxBattery.Notes: EU4 is CPU-bound for simulation logic, not GPU-bound; a low GPU clock and TDP cap are safe here. The 30 fps cap and 40 Hz refresh rate keep power draw minimal while the game remains fully playable as a turn-based-style strategy title.

KnownIssues: No native controller support — players must rely on the Steam Deck's trackpads and on-screen keyboard, which can be cumbersome for a complex strategy UI.
Small UI text and map details may be difficult to read on the 7-inch 1280x800 screen without zooming in.
Long late-game sessions with large mod lists or complex saves can cause CPU-side slowdowns as the simulation scales up.
Occasional Proton compatibility quirks reported (gold/platinum tier); using Proton Experimental or GE-Proton may resolve edge cases.

MaxPerformance.Notes: EU4's renderer is light enough that the Deck can run it uncapped at max settings without breaking a sweat on the GPU side; the primary bottleneck in late-game is CPU simulation speed, not frame rate. Full TDP is overkill here but ensures the CPU boosts freely for fast simulation speed.

Optimal.Notes: The game runs comfortably at medium settings and native resolution with a stable 60 fps; UI scaling at 125% makes the map and menus much more readable on the Deck's 7-inch screen. This is the recommended everyday profile.
